newsitem.title: UK: Stong grinds fuel LIFFE cocoa but volume thin.
newsitem.headline: Stong grinds fuel LIFFE cocoa but volume thin.

text.p: London cocoa futures received a sudden boost from surprisingly strong UK and Dutch third quarter grinds on Friday, but there were few players to act on the news.
The UK grind, up 42 percent from a year ago at 48,855 tonnes, outpaced even the wildest guesses. One industry estimate last week of around 20 percent was said to be conditional.
"I don't think anybody was expecting such a big number," commented one trader on the UK grind.
But turnover was modest at 1,942 lots with many operators leaving for a Paris trade dinner on Friday.
The most active March contract jumped to the psychological barrier of 1,000 stg but closed off the high at 995 stg a tonne, a rise of 10 stg on the day.
Earlier, the Dutch Cocoa Association (NCV) put the local grind at 99,549 tonnes in the third quarter, up 16.69 percent from a year ago. The market's expectation was around 10 percent.
"It's a hell of a grind," said another trader referring to the Dutch figure. "It's very, very bullish."

The UK grind is believed to have been partly helped by the resumption of production at the leading chocolate maker Mars. The year-ago grindings, the worst quarter in 1995, were affected by the closure of that plant.
Traders said the timing of the grind figures was unfortunate as the market failed to pick up momentum to pierce resistance.
"It need to clear levels higher than this to attract some big short-covering," said one trader. "There is quite a substantial resistance."
Technical analysts said the market would need to go through 1,025 stg at least for the outlook to improve.
